Why a night train can cost more than a flight

By Priya Raman · Analysis

Sleeper tickets are often dearer than a budget flight on the same route. The reasons lie in how night trains are run.

Track access charges are paid for every kilometre, and night trains cover long distances with few passengers per carriage.

Staff work through the night, carriages stand idle during the day, and beds take far more space than seats.

Airlines, by contrast, pay no fuel tax on international flights in most countries.
